techniques.name: CDNs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search content delivery network (CDN) data about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Scan Databases
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search within public scan databases for information about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Search Closed Sources
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search and gather information about victims from closed (e.g., paid, private, or otherwise not freely available) sources that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Threat Intel Vendors
techniques.summary: Adversaries may search private data from threat intelligence vendors for information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Purchase Technical Data
techniques.summary: Adversaries may purchase technical information about victims that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send phishing messages to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages via third-party services to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages with a malicious attachment to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Link
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages with a malicious link to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Voice
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use voice communications to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Network Boundary Bridging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bridge network boundaries by compromising perimeter network devices or internal devices responsible for network segmentation.

techniques.name: Network Address Translation Traversal
techniques.summary: Adversaries may bridge network boundaries by modifying a network device’s Network Address Translation (NAT) configuration.

techniques.name: Weaken Encryption
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise a network device’s encryption capability in order to bypass encryption that would otherwise protect data communications.

techniques.name: Reduce Key Space
techniques.summary: Adversaries may reduce the level of effort required to decrypt data transmitted over the network by reducing the cipher strength of encrypted communications.

techniques.name: Disable Crypto Hardware
techniques.summary: Adversaries disable a network device’s dedicated hardware encryption, which may enable them to leverage weaknesses in software encryption in order to reduce the effort involved in collecting, manipulating, and exfiltrating transmitted data.

techniques.name: Modify System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may make changes to the operating system of embedded network devices to weaken defenses and provide new capabilities for themselves.

techniques.name: Patch System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the operating system of a network device to introduce new capabilities or weaken existing defenses.

techniques.name: Downgrade System Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install an older version of the operating system of a network device to weaken security.

techniques.name: Data from Configuration Repository
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect data related to managed devices from configuration repositories.

techniques.name: SNMP (MIB Dump)
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target the Management Information Base (MIB) to collect and/or mine valuable information in a network managed using Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP).

techniques.name: Network Device Configuration Dump
techniques.summary: Adversaries may access network configuration files to collect sensitive data about the device and the network.

techniques.name: Forge Web Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forge credential materials that can be used to gain access to web applications or Internet services.

techniques.name: Web Cookies
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forge web cookies that can be used to gain access to web applications or Internet services.

techniques.name: SAML Tokens
techniques.summary: An adversary may forge SAML tokens with any permissions claims and lifetimes if they possess a valid SAML token-signing certificate.

techniques.name: Stage Capabilities
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload, install, or otherwise set up capabilities that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Upload Malware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload malware to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting.

techniques.name: Upload Tool
techniques.summary: Adversaries may upload tools to third-party or adversary controlled infrastructure to make it accessible during targeting.

techniques.name: Install Digital Certificate
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install SSL/TLS certificates that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Drive-by Target
techniques.summary: Adversaries may prepare an operational environment to infect systems that visit a website over the normal course of browsing.

techniques.name: Link Target
techniques.summary: Adversaries may put in place resources that are referenced by a link that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: SEO Poisoning
techniques.summary: Adversaries may poison mechanisms that influence search engine optimization (SEO) to further lure staged capabilities towards potential victims.

techniques.name: Container Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse a container administration service to execute commands within a container.

techniques.name: Deploy Container
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deploy a container into an environment to facilitate execution or evade defenses.

techniques.name: Escape to Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may break out of a container or virtualized environment to gain access to the underlying host.

techniques.name: Build Image on Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may build a container image directly on a host to bypass defenses that monitor for the retrieval of malicious images from a public registry.

techniques.name: Container and Resource Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to discover containers and other resources that are available within a containers environment.

techniques.name: System Location Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information in an attempt to calculate the geographical location of a victim host.

techniques.name: System Language Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about the system language of a victim in order to infer the geographical location of that host.

techniques.name: Group Policy Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information on Group Policy settings to identify paths for privilege escalation, security measures applied within a domain, and to discover patterns in domain objects that can be manipulated or used to blend in the environment.

techniques.name: Cloud Storage Object Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate objects in cloud storage infrastructure.

techniques.name: Reflective Code Loading
techniques.summary: Adversaries may reflectively load code into a process in order to conceal the execution of malicious payloads.

techniques.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanisms and gain access to accounts by generating MFA requests sent to users.

techniques.name: Debugger Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various means to detect and avoid debuggers.

techniques.name: Plist File Modification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify property list files (plist files) to enable other malicious activity, while also potentially evading and bypassing system defenses.

techniques.name: Serverless Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse serverless computing, integration, and automation services to execute arbitrary code in cloud environments.

techniques.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal or forge certificates used for authentication to access remote systems or resources.

techniques.name: Acquire Access
techniques.summary: Adversaries may purchase or otherwise acquire an existing access to a target system or network.

techniques.name: Cloud Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse cloud management services to execute commands within virtual machines.

techniques.name: Device Driver Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to enumerate local device drivers on a victim host.

techniques.name: Power Settings
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impair a system's ability to hibernate, reboot, or shut down in order to extend access to infected machines.

techniques.name: Log Enumeration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate system and service logs to find useful data.

techniques.name: Impersonation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impersonate a trusted person or organization in order to persuade and trick a target into performing some action on their behalf.

techniques.name: Financial Theft
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal monetary resources from targets through extortion, social engineering, technical theft, or other methods aimed at their own financial gain at the expense of the availability of these resources for victims.

techniques.name: Content Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access and continuously communicate with victims by injecting malicious content into systems through online network traffic.

techniques.name: Hide Infrastructure
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate network traffic in order to hide and evade detection of their C2 infrastructure.

techniques.name: Modify Cloud Resource Hierarchy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to modify hierarchical structures in infrastructure-as-a-service (IaaS) environments in order to evade defenses.

techniques.name: Email Bombing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may flood targeted email addresses with an overwhelming volume of messages.

techniques.name: Exclusive Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries who successfully compromise a system may attempt to maintain persistence by “closing the door” behind them – in other words, by preventing other threat actors from initially accessing or maintaining a foothold on the same system.

techniques.name: Wi-Fi Networks
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain initial access to target systems by connecting to wireless networks.

techniques.name: Cloud Application Integration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may achieve persistence by leveraging OAuth application integrations in a software-as-a-service environment.

techniques.name: Email Spoofing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may fake, or spoof, a sender’s identity by modifying the value of relevant email headers in order to establish contact with victims under false pretenses.

techniques.name: Virtual Machine Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to enumerate running virtual machines (VMs) after gaining access to a host or hypervisor.

techniques.name: Input Injection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may simulate keystrokes on a victim’s computer by various means to perform any type of action on behalf of the user, such as launching the command interpreter using keyboard shortcuts, typing an inline script to be executed, or interacting directly with a GUI-based application.

techniques.name: ESXi Administration Command
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse ESXi administration services to execute commands on guest machines hosted within an ESXi virtual environment.

techniques.name: Poisoned Pipeline Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate continuous integration / continuous development (CI/CD) processes by injecting malicious code into the build process.

techniques.name: Delay Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may employ various time-based methods to evade detection and analysis.

techniques.name: Selective Exclusion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may intentionally exclude certain files, folders, directories, file types, or system components from encryption or tampering during a ransomware or malicious payload execution.

techniques.name: Local Storage Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may enumerate local drives, disks, and/or volumes and their attributes like total or free space and volume serial number.

techniques.name: Search Threat Vendor Data
techniques.summary: Threat actors may seek information/indicators from closed or open threat intelligence sources gathered about their own campaigns, as well as those conducted by other adversaries that may align with their target industries, capabilities/objectives, or other operational concerns.

techniques.name: Query Public AI Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may query publicly accessible artificial intelligence (AI) services, such as large language models (LLMs), to support targeting and operations.

techniques.name: Generate Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or generate content to support targeting and operations.

techniques.name: Written Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or tailor written materials to support targeting and malicious operations.

techniques.name: Audio-Visual Content
techniques.summary: Adversaries may create or manipulate audio, image, and video content to support targeting and malicious operations.

techniques.name: Social Engineering
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use social engineering techniques to influence users to take actions that result in unauthorized access, approval of changes, disclosure of sensitive information, or execution of adversary-supplied instructions (i.e., introduction of malicious payloads or software), while minimizing technical indicators.

techniques.name: Impersonation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impersonate a trusted person or organization in order to persuade and trick a target into performing some action on their behalf.

techniques.name: Email Spoofing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may fake, or spoof, a sender’s identity by modifying the value of relevant email headers in order to establish contact with victims under false pretenses.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable, degrade, or tamper with security tools or applications (e.g., endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools, intrusion detection systems (IDS), antivirus, logging agents, sensors, etc.) to impair or reduce visibility of defensive capabilities.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Windows Event Log to limit data that can be leveraged for detections and audits.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
techniques.summary: An adversary may disable or modify cloud logging capabilities and integrations to limit what data is collected on their activities and avoid detection.

techniques.name: Modify or Spoof Tool UI
techniques.summary: Adversaries may spoof or manipulate security tool user interfaces (UIs) to falsely indicate tools are functioning normally and delay detection and response.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Linux Audit System Log
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Linux Audit system to hide malicious activity and avoid detection.

techniques.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may clear Windows Event Logs to hide the activity of an intrusion.

techniques.name: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
techniques.summary: Adversaries may clear system logs to hide evidence of an intrusion.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify host-based or network firewalls to impair defensive mechanisms and enable further action.

techniques.name: Cloud Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify a firewall within a cloud environment to bypass controls that limit access to cloud resources.

techniques.name: Network Device Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable network device-based firewall mechanisms entirely or add, delete, or modify particular rules in order to bypass controls limiting network usage.

techniques.name: Windows Host Firewall
techniques.summary: Adversaries may disable or modify the Windows host firewall to bypass controls limiting network usage.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Defense Impairment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in security software, infrastructure, or defensive components to degrade, disable, or otherwise continue to impair their ability to prevent, detect, or respond to malicious activity.

techniques.name: Safe Mode Boot
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse Windows safe mode to disable endpoint defenses.

techniques.name: Downgrade Attack
techniques.summary: Adversaries may downgrade or use a version of system features that may be outdated, vulnerable, and/or does not support updated security controls.

techniques.name: Prevent Command History Logging
techniques.summary: Adversaries may impair command history logging to hide commands they run on a compromised system.

techniques.name: Activate Firmware Update Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may activate firmware update mode on devices to prevent expected response functions from engaging in reaction to an emergency or process malfunction.

techniques.name: Monitor Process State
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information about the physical process state.

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may automate collection of industrial environment information using tools or scripts.

techniques.name: Block Command Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block a command message from reaching its intended target to prevent command execution.

techniques.name: Block Reporting Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block or prevent a reporting message from reaching its intended target.

techniques.name: Block Serial COM
techniques.summary: Adversaries may block access to serial COM to prevent instructions or configurations from reaching target devices.

techniques.name: Brute Force I/O
techniques.summary: Adversaries may repetitively or successively change I/O point values to perform an action.

techniques.name: Command-Line Interface
techniques.summary: Adversaries may utilize command-line interfaces (CLIs) to interact with systems and execute commands.

techniques.name: Control Device Identification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform control device identification to determine the make and model of a target device.

techniques.name: Data Destruction
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform data destruction over the course of an operation.

techniques.name: Data Historian Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise and gain control of a data historian to gain a foothold into the control system environment.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from information repositories.

techniques.name: Default Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage manufacturer or supplier set default credentials on control system devices.

techniques.name: Denial of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of control to temporarily prevent operators and engineers from interacting with process controls.

techniques.name: Denial of Service
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks to disrupt expected device functionality.

techniques.name: Denial of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a denial of view in attempt to disrupt and prevent operator oversight on the status of an ICS environment.

techniques.name: Device Restart/Shutdown
techniques.summary: Adversaries may forcibly restart or shutdown a device in an ICS environment to disrupt and potentially negatively impact physical processes.

techniques.name: Drive-by Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access to a system during a drive-by compromise, when a user visits a website as part of a regular browsing session.

techniques.name: Engineering Workstation Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries will compromise and gain control of an engineering workstation for Initial Access into the control system environment.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage weaknesses to exploit internet-facing software for initial access into an industrial network.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Evasion
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to evade detection.

techniques.name: Modify Controller Tasking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify the tasking of a controller to allow for the execution of their own programs.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage external remote services as a point of initial access into your network.

techniques.name: Graphical User Interface
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to gain access to a machine via a Graphical User Interface (GUI) to enhance execution capabilities.

techniques.name: I/O Module Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use input/output (I/O) module discovery to gather key information about a control system device.

techniques.name: Location Identification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform location identification using device data to inform operations and targeted impact for attacks.

techniques.name: Loss of Availability
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to disrupt essential components or systems to prevent owner and operator from delivering products or services.

techniques.name: Loss of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to achieve a sustained loss of control or a runaway condition in which operators cannot issue any commands even if the malicious interference has subsided.

techniques.name: Loss of Productivity and Revenue
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause loss of productivity and revenue through disruption and even damage to the availability and integrity of control system operations, devices, and related processes.

techniques.name: Loss of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause a sustained or permanent loss of view where the ICS equipment will require local, hands-on operator intervention; for instance, a restart or manual operation.

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
techniques.summary: Adversaries with privileged network access may seek to modify network traffic in real time using adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks.

techniques.name: Manipulation of Control
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate physical process control within the industrial environment.

techniques.name: Manipulation of View
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate the information reported back to operators or controllers.

techniques.name: Modify Control Logic
techniques.summary: Adversaries may place malicious code in a system, which can cause the system to malfunction by modifying its control logic.

techniques.name: Native API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may directly interact with the native OS application programming interface (API) to access system functions.

techniques.name: Manipulate I/O Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may manipulate the I/O image of PLCs through various means to prevent them from functioning as expected.

techniques.name: Modify Parameter
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify parameters used to instruct industrial control system devices.

techniques.name: Loss of Protection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise protective system functions designed to prevent the effects of faults and abnormal conditions.

techniques.name: Modify Alarm Settings
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify alarm settings to prevent alerts that may inform operators of their presence or to prevent responses to dangerous and unintended scenarios.

techniques.name: Module Firmware
techniques.summary: Adversaries may install malicious or vulnerable firmware onto modular hardware devices.

techniques.name: Network Connection Enumeration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform network connection enumeration to discover information about device communication patterns.

techniques.name: Network Service Scanning
techniques.summary: Network Service Scanning is the process of discovering services on networked systems.

techniques.name: Network Sniffing
techniques.summary: Network sniffing is the practice of using a network interface on a computer system to monitor or capture information regardless of whether it is the specified destination for the information.

techniques.name: Program Download
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform a program download to transfer a user program to a controller.

techniques.name: Download All
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute a full program download to a PLC to overwrite the entire PLC program and configuration to deploy a new project or make major changes.

techniques.name: Online Edit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute an online edit of a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

techniques.name: Program Append
techniques.summary: Adversaries may execute a program append to a PLC to update parts of an existing program.

techniques.name: Program Organization Units
techniques.summary: Program Organizational Units (POUs) are block structures used within PLC programming to create programs and projects.

techniques.name: Program Upload
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to upload a program from a PLC to gather information about an industrial process.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for subsequent Lateral Movement or Discovery techniques.

techniques.name: Port Scan
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform a port scan on a system, device, or network to identify live hosts, enumerate open ports and running services, identify operating systems, and map out the network.

techniques.name: Broadcast Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform broadcast discovery requests to enumerate systems and devices on a network.

techniques.name: Multicast Discovery
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform multicast discovery requests which is when one system or device sends messages to all systems and devices in a pre-defined group on a network (or subnet) and then waits for a response.

techniques.name: Replication Through Removable Media
techniques.summary: Adversaries may move onto systems, such as those separated from the enterprise network, by copying malware to removable media which is inserted into the control systems environment.

techniques.name: Rogue Master
techniques.summary: Adversaries may setup a rogue master to leverage control server functions to communicate with outstations.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use masquerading to disguise a malicious application or executable as another file, to avoid operator and engineer suspicion.

techniques.name: Role Identification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform role identification of devices involved with physical processes of interest in a target control system.

techniques.name: Rootkit
techniques.summary: Adversaries may deploy rootkits to hide the presence of programs, files, network connections, services, drivers, and other system components.

techniques.name: Screen Capture
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to perform screen capture of devices in the control system environment.

techniques.name: Scripting
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use scripting languages to execute arbitrary code in the form of a pre-written script or in the form of user-supplied code to an interpreter.

techniques.name: Serial Connection Enumeration
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform serial connection enumeration to gather situational awareness after gaining access to devices in the OT network.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may send unauthorized command messages to instruct control system assets to perform actions outside of their intended functionality, or without the logical preconditions to trigger their expected function.

techniques.name: Spoof Reporting Message
techniques.summary: Adversaries may spoof reporting messages in control system environments for evasion and to impair process control.

techniques.name: System Firmware
techniques.summary: System firmware on modern assets is often designed with an update feature.

techniques.name: Change Operating Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may change the operating mode of a controller to gain additional access to engineering functions such as Program Download.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal the credentials of a specific user or service account using credential access techniques.

techniques.name: Wireless Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform wireless compromise as a method of gaining communications and unauthorized access to a wireless network.

techniques.name: Point & Tag Identification
techniques.summary: Adversaries may collect point and tag values to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the process environment.

techniques.name: Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.summary: Adversaries may perform supply chain compromise to gain control systems environment access by means of infected products, software, and workflows.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.summary: Adversaries may rely on a targeted organizations user interaction for the execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Transient Cyber Asset
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target devices that are transient across ICS networks and external networks.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a spearphishing attachment, a variant of spearphishing, as a form of a social engineering attack against specific targets.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit a software vulnerability to take advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to enable remote service abuse.

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.summary: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from one system to another to stage adversary tools or other files over the course of an operation.

techniques.name: Detect Operating Mode
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gather information about a PLCs or controllers current operating mode.

techniques.name: Standard Application Layer Protocol
techniques.summary: Adversaries may establish command and control capabilities over commonly used application layer protocols such as HTTP(S), OPC, RDP, telnet, DNP3, and modbus.

techniques.name: Detect Program State
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to gather information about the current state of a program on a PLC.

techniques.name: Execution through API
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to leverage Application Program Interfaces (APIs) used for communication between control software and the hardware.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal on Host
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to remove indicators of their presence on a system in an effort to cover their tracks.

techniques.name: Project File Infection
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to infect project files with malicious code.

techniques.name: Siemens Project File Format

techniques.name: Hooking
techniques.summary: Adversaries may hook into application programming interface (API) functions used by processes to redirect calls for execution and privilege escalation means.

techniques.name: Change Program State
techniques.summary: Adversaries may attempt to change the state of the current program on a control device.

techniques.name: I/O Image
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture process values related to the inputs and outputs of a PLC.

techniques.name: Alarm Suppression
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target protection function alarms to prevent them from notifying operators of critical conditions.

techniques.name: Damage to Property
techniques.summary: Adversaries may cause damage and destruction of property to infrastructure, equipment, and the surrounding environment when attacking control systems.

techniques.name: Loss of Safety
techniques.summary: Adversaries may compromise safety system functions designed to maintain safe operation of a process when unacceptable or dangerous conditions occur.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.summary: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable to legitimate users.

techniques.name: Theft of Operational Information
techniques.summary: Adversaries may steal operational information on a production environment as a direct mission outcome for personal gain or to inform future operations.

techniques.name: Internet Accessible Device
techniques.summary: Adversaries may gain access into industrial environments through systems exposed directly to the internet for remote access rather than through [External Remote Services](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T0822).

techniques.name: Connection Proxy
techniques.summary: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or act as an intermediary for network communications.

techniques.name: Commonly Used Port
techniques.summary: Adversaries may communicate over a commonly used port to bypass firewalls or network detection systems and to blend in with normal network activity, to avoid more detailed inspection.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage remote services to move between assets and network segments.

techniques.name: Wireless Sniffing
techniques.summary: Adversaries may seek to capture radio frequency (RF) communication used for remote control and reporting in distributed environments.

techniques.name: Remote System Information Discovery
techniques.summary: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about remote systems and their peripherals, such as make/model, role, and configuration.

techniques.name: Modify Program
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify or add a program on a controller to affect how it interacts with the physical process, peripheral devices and other hosts on the network.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.summary: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.

techniques.name: Hardcoded Credentials
techniques.summary: Adversaries may leverage credentials that are hardcoded in software or firmware to gain an unauthorized interactive user session to an asset.

techniques.name: Change Credential
techniques.summary: Adversaries may modify software and device credentials to prevent operator and responder access.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.summary: Adversaries may target and collect data from local system sources, such as file systems, configuration files, or local databases.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution

techniques.name: Linked Devices
techniques.summary: Adversaries may abuse the “linked devices” feature on messaging applications, such as Signal and WhatsApp, to register the user’s account to an adversary-controlled device.
